anchor: The 1740s-1830s evangelical revival sermon as a printed object: old-style American letterpress with the devotional printer's rubrication (black ink + a single red), the New-Birth sunburst woodcut on the title page, and the camp-meeting broadside, all on laid cream rag paper.
rationale: The Awakenings were spread and contested through print — Edwards's 'A Faithful Narrative' (1737), Whitefield's serialized 'Journals' and newspaper machine, Chauncy's 'Seasonable Thoughts' (1743), Finney's 'Lectures on Revivals' (1835). Their controlling image is the New Birth as light breaking — the 'sun of righteousness,' Edwards's 'divine and supernatural light,' the recurring 'outpouring.' So: a rubricated letterpress page (ink black + sermon-rubric vermilion) lit by a sunburst gilt, with a sober Old-Light slate as the critical counter-pole and a 'burned-over' field green — the corpus's own both/and (revival heat vs. sober critique) rendered as two tinctures against fire.
